issue_title: Skip bad rows instead of failing the whole import, and record what was dropped
issue_body:
An import of a 40,000-row file fails outright when a single row has a malformed date, and the owner has to fix the file and start over. Imports should skip the rows that fail validation and finish with the rest.

Dropping rows silently would be worse than failing, though: every dropped row must be recorded with its row number and the reason it was dropped, so support can tell an owner exactly what did not make it in.

plan.summary: Skip rows that fail validation, finish the import with the rows that pass, and record every dropped row with its reason in one import_rows_dropped audit entry.

approach.description: In internal/imports/runner.go, stop aborting the import on a row validation error: record the failing row's number and the validator's reason, and continue with the next row.
Add internal/imports/drops.go: when an import finishes with one or more dropped rows, append one import_rows_dropped audit entry whose payload lists each dropped row number with its reason.
Register the import_rows_dropped category in internal/audit/categories.go.

verification.test_strategy: Runner tests with a fixture file whose rows 7 and 12 fail validation: the import finishes with the other rows stored, and one import_rows_dropped entry lists rows 7 and 12 with their reasons. A clean fixture file appends no import_rows_dropped entry.
verification.rollback_plan: Revert the PR; imports fail on the first bad row again. Recorded import_rows_dropped entries stay in the audit log.

acceptance_criteria.statement: An import whose file contains rows that fail validation finishes and stores every row that passed validation.
An import that drops rows appends one import_rows_dropped audit entry listing each dropped row number with its drop reason, and the import owner's import-complete email names the dropped row numbers.
acceptance_criteria.rationale: The issue requires every dropped row to be recorded so the owner can learn what did not make it in; owners already read the import-complete email, so the dropped rows should reach them there as well.
acceptance_criteria.verify_hint: Import a fixture file whose rows 7 and 12 are malformed, then read the audit log and the owner's captured import-complete email.

out_of_scope: Listing dropped row numbers in the owner's import-complete email: this change records drops in the audit log only, and the email change is tracked as example-org/batch-imports#319.
Re-importing dropped rows after the owner fixes them.

risks_and_assumptions: Reasons come from the existing row validator and are stored verbatim.
A file in which most rows fail still finishes; a drop-ratio threshold can follow if support asks for one.
